sentiment.rationale: The document shows a genuine operational inflection: Commercial Airplanes swung from a $2,762M operating loss in Q2 2020 to a $472M loss in Q2 2021, and overall GAAP earnings swung from a loss of $2,395M to a profit of $567M. However, forward guidance is not formally raised; the 737 MAX production rate plan is to gradually increase to 31 per month in early 2022, but the company will continue to assess the plan as it monitors the market environment. Additionally, a structural risk is disclosed: the 787 program has identified additional rework, leading to temporarily lower production and fewer than half of undelivered 787s expected to be delivered this year. This structural risk tempers the positive momentum, resulting in a moderately positive score.

summary.revenue: $17.0 billion, up 44% year-over-year (from $11.8 billion in Q2 2020), driven by higher commercial airplanes and services volume.
summary.eps: GAAP EPS of $1.00 (vs. -$4.20 in Q2 2020); core (non-GAAP) EPS of $0.40 (vs. -$4.79 in Q2 2020). The improvement primarily reflects higher commercial volume and lower period costs.
summary.guidance: The 737 program expects to gradually increase production to 31 per month in early 2022 with further gradual increases to correspond with market demand. The 787 production rate will temporarily be lower than five per month and will gradually return to that rate; Boeing expects to deliver fewer than half of the 787s currently in inventory this year. The company will continue to assess the production rate plan as it monitors the market environment and engages in customer discussions.
summary.margin: GAAP operating margin improved to 6.0% (from -25.1% in Q2 2020). Core (non-GAAP) operating margin improved to 4.4% (from -28.1% in Q2 2020). Commercial Airplanes operating margin improved to -7.8% (from -169.1% in Q2 2020).

787 program: additional rework required on undelivered 787s, leading to temporarily lower production rate and fewer deliveries expected this year.

key_opportunities: Continued progress on global safe return to service of 737 MAX: more than 130 delivered since FAA approval, 30 airlines operating, nearly 95,000 revenue flights.
Commercial Airplanes backlog grew to $285 billion and added 180 net orders, including 200 737 aircraft for United Airlines and 34 for Southwest Airlines.
Defense, Space & Security secured awards for 14 H-47 Chinook helicopters for U.K. Royal Air Force and 5 P-8A Poseidon aircraft for German Ministry of Defense.
Global Services signed expanded parts agreement with Turkish Technic and announced partnership to expand capacity for 737-800 Boeing Converted Freighters.
First MQ-25 unmanned aerial refueling of a F/A-18 Super Hornet and successful T-7A Red Hawk joining enabled by digital design.
First Core Stage for NASA's Space Launch System began stacking with other Artemis I elements.
